name: TX-26
label: Safe R

key_factors: First-term incumbent with no outside opposition spending
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean, Gill's overwhelming financial advantage, and Polymarket pricing him at 97% all point to a safe Republican hold; the Democrat has raised almost nothing. A modest shift toward Gill from the baseline is justified by the lopsided money gap and absence of any opposing outside spending.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected late-breaking outside spending against Gill could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brandon Gill, a first-term Republican incumbent, is heavily favored in this North Texas district, which leans Republican by about 11 points. He has raised more than $4.2 million and holds $1.4 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Steven Shook has raised under $20,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against Gill, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Gill roughly a 97% chance of winning, and no public general-election polling exists. With the incumbent well-funded, unchallenged by outside money, and running in a strongly favorable environment, the race is rated Safe Republican.
